text:
Ana: Hi all, first day! Quick checklist: got Homebrew on M2, installed asdf, cloned dotfiles. Running into two probs: (1) the repo devcontainer wants python 3.9 but `asdf` installed 3.11, and (2) local Postgres version mismatch with CI. Any minimal steps to get a reproducible dev env?

Ravi: Congrats and welcome! For python, check if repo has `.tool-versions` — `asdf install` will pick it up. If not, set `asdf local python 3.9.13` in the repo dir. Mac M2 can build slower; try `brew install openssl readline sqlite3` first.

Ana: I don't see `.tool-versions`. Is it okay to add one? Don't want to break others.

Claire: Yep add it. We pin runtime in repo for reproducibility. Commit a change like `echo "python 3.9.13" > .tool-versions` and open a tiny PR.

Ana: Nice. Postgres? CI runs 14, mac brew gave me 15 by default.

Ravi: Use `pg_ctl` from the asdf-postgres plugin or install via `brew install postgres@14` and then `brew services start postgres@14`. Then adjust PATH: `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/postgres@14/bin:$PATH"`.

Ana: I'm running inside the VS Code devcontainer though. The container image has Postgres 14 but my host also has 15 and `psql` points to host. How do folks avoid conflicts when using the container?

DevEx: Two ways, pick one: (A) Use the container's terminal for DB work so `psql` comes from container; or (B) install `pg` client via `brew install libpq` and then `brew link --force libpq` to get `psql` on host. We prefer A to avoid host drift. Add a `.vscode/settings.json` entry to set the default terminal to the container.

Ana: Got it. Also setting up git/ssh: my SSH key is on 1Password and I normally use the 1p CLI. Any Redwood convention for signing commits or GPG?

Claire: We don't mandate commit signing for new-hires, but if you have a YubiKey use it. For 1Password CLI: `eval $(op signin)` then `op item get "redwood/ssh-key" --out-file ~/.ssh/id_rsa && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa`. For GPG commit signing we document keys in handbook.

Ana: Thanks. One more: dotfiles use `direnv` but my shell is fish; direnv example is bash. How to make it work?

Ravi: For fish add `status --is-interactive; and source (direnv hook fish)` to `~/.config/fish/config.fish`. Also ensure `.envrc` uses POSIX-compatible commands or add a `use fish` wrapper in the repo.

infra-bot: Onboarding tip: we updated the devcontainer template last week to include python 3.9 and postgres 14, and added a `dev-setup.md` snippet. https://go.redwood/handbook/dev-setup

Ana: Perfect. I'll add the `.tool-versions` and a tiny note about fish hooks in the dotfiles PR. One last micro-ask: where do I put environment secrets locally? `.envrc` sample or 1Password?

DevEx: Store creds in 1Password and pull them into env via `op` inside your `.envrc` like: `export DATABASE_URL=$(op item get "redwood/dev-db" --fields password)` and keep `.envrc` out of git. We also prefer `direnv` for gating.

Ana: Thanks team — I'll open the PR and ping for reviews. Appreciate the fast help!
